WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT t1.id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants t1
  WHERE t1.name = 'Deskline Supplies'
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    s.carrier AS carrier,
    s.service_level AS service_level,
    s.shipping_cost AS shipping_cost,
    COALESCE(s.currency_code, tn.default_currency_code) AS ship_currency_code,
    s.shipped_at AS shipped_at
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  JOIN t0 ON t0.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
  JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = s.tenant_id
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t2.carrier AS carrier,
    t2.service_level AS service_level,
    t2.shipping_cost AS shipping_cost,
    CASE
      WHEN t2.ship_currency_code = 'EUR' THEN t2.shipping_cost
      ELSE t2.shipping_cost / er.rate
    END AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM t2
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = t2.ship_currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(t2.shipped_at AS date)
)
SELECT
  t3.carrier AS carrier,
  t3.service_level AS service_level,
  COUNT(*) AS shipment_count_2025,
  ROUND(SUM(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS total_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS avg_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(MIN(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS min_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(MAX(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS max_shipping_cost_eur
FROM t3
GROUP BY t3.carrier, t3.service_level
ORDER BY total_shipping_cost_eur DESC, t3.carrier ASC, t3.service_level ASC
note: Shipments joined via fulfillments->orders to filter to Deskline Supplies' tenant_id, limited to shipped_at in 2025, with shipping_cost converted to EUR using exchange_rates (EUR base, shipment's own currency_code, falling back to the tenant's default currency if the shipment row has none) at the as_of date matching shipped_at's calendar day. Min/max per carrier+service_level lane should make it easy to spot whether the high average is driven by a few outlier shipments or a broad pattern.
